challenge.name: broken authentication control (TODO OR NOT TODO)

all_of: a listing endpoint takes the identity to list as a path segment rather than deriving it from the session
the caller already holds a valid session and any per-session secret the endpoint requires
any_of: a comment, disabled control or dead code in the page names a special value for that segment
the endpoint accepts a collective value such as all in place of an identity

chain.action: read the entry page including its inline script and hidden inputs, not only the linked JavaScript
chain.why: the per-session secret, the identity to use and a comment naming the unpatched check were all inline in the page

chain.action: list every API route from the linked JavaScript and note which ones take an identity in the path
chain.why: an identity in the path is the bug surface; an identity taken from the session is not

chain.action: call the listing endpoint for your own identity and record the exact response
chain.why: an empty own-listing is what makes a populated response for another value proof rather than a guess

chain.action: replace only the identity segment with the collective value the page hinted at, keeping the same cookie and secret
chain.why: the special value is handled upstream of the ownership comparison, so nothing has to be forged or enumerated

first_confirming_probe.request: issue the listing request twice with one cookie and one secret, once for your own identity and once with the identity segment replaced by the collective value
first_confirming_probe.expected: your own listing is empty or short while the collective value returns rows owned by another account
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the collective value returns the same rows as your own identity, or is rejected with the same error as an unrelated identity

blast_radius: read-only. Use the listing route only; the same API exposes completion and deletion routes that take an id and would mutate another account's objects, so never point those at an id that is not yours.

verification.evidence: the flag was returned as the name field of one object in the JSON array from the listing endpoint on the live target

reuse_when: a route embeds a username, account id or tenant in the path while the session already identifies the caller
front-end code or a comment mentions a value for that segment which the interface never sends
an application provisions a throwaway identity per visit instead of offering a login
known_traps: the session cookie, the identity and the per-session secret are issued together on each visit; pairing a stale identity with a fresh cookie returns an authorisation error that looks exactly like the control working, which is a false negative that can kill a correct hypothesis
capture the cookie, the identity and the secret from one single response before probing
the session cookie is signed and does not need to be forged; the bug is entirely in the path segment
